BARCELONA, Nov 22 : Barcelona shook off a sloppy first half to beat Villarreal 3-2 in LaLiga on Sunday. Villarreal raced into a two-goal lead after seven minutes, as Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi took advantage of lax Barcelona play early on. Lamine Yamal won a penalty midway through the first half, but dragged the spot-kick onto the post in the 23rd minute. Gerard Martin headed in a Pedri cross in the 57th minute to reduce the gap, before Fermin Lopez equalised four minutes later.

Barcelona's third followed in quick succession when Villarreal defender Pau Navarro turned Lamine Yamal's cross into his own goal. Navarro was then sent off for a second yellow in stoppage time. Barcelona remain top of the standings on 36 points, three ahead of Real Madrid after Jose Mourinho's side beat Celta Vigo on Saturday. Villarreal remain ninth on 15 points.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Rep. McCaul Seeks Answers From Jensen Huang
item.description: Republican Congressman Michael McCaul tells Bloomberg This Weekend that he wants answers from Nvidia’s Jensen Huang about the company’s chip sales and whether advanced AI technology reached China in violation of US export controls, amid scrutiny of Huang’s relationship with a woman accused of ties to Chinese intelligence. LAS VEGAS, Nov 22 : Formula One stewards handed Mexican Sergio Perez a five-place grid penalty for next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix after ruling the Cadillac driver caused a collision with Haas' Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara in Las Vegas on Saturday. • Perez would have collected a 10 second penalty but because he had retired from the race it was changed to a grid drop for his next race instead • The stewards said Perez had not earned the right to the corner and was wholly to blame for the lap 18 collision on approaching turn 14 • "I was alongside him and expected him to leave me enough room to make the corner," said Perez. "I was planning to make the move afterwards, into Turn 16, but unfortunately he didn’t see me. By the time I tried to avoid him, it was already too late. He apologised afterwards and explained that he simply hadn’t seen me."

item.title: ¿Cuáles fueron las 10 OPI con mayores alzas en su debut? Anthropic y SpaceX, fuera del listado
item.description: El 2026 quedará marcado en Wall Street por los debuts bursátiles de Anthropic PBC (ANT) y SpaceX (SPCX), que protagonizaron las dos mayores ofertas públicas iniciales (OPI) de la historia. Anthropic ...
item.dc:creator: Juan Pablo Álvarez
item.content:encoded: El 2026 quedará marcado en Wall Street por los debuts bursátiles de Anthropic PBC ( ANT ) y SpaceX ( SPCX ), que protagonizaron las dos mayores ofertas públicas iniciales (OPI) de la historia. Anthropic superó el récord de recaudación establecido previamente por la compañía de Elon Musk. Sin embargo, ninguna de las dos figura entre las diez empresas cuyas acciones registraron las mayores subidas durante su primera jornada de cotización. Un informe de la plataforma global de inversiones XTB identificó las diez OPI con los mayores avances en su debut bursátil. El ranking está dominado casi por completo por compañías que comenzaron a cotizar durante el auge tecnológico de 1999 y 2000, en plena burbuja de las puntocom. La única excepción es Newsmax, que debutó en bolsa en marzo de 2025 y registró un alza del 735,1% durante su primera jornada. Sin embargo, la euforia fue pasajera: desde entonces, sus acciones han perdido más del 90% de su valor. VER MÁS: Un dato importante es que ninguna de las compañías mencionadas logró mantener en el tiempo el precio alcanzado en el primer día de negociación “Las mayores subidas durante una salida a bolsa no necesariamente corresponden a las empresas que más dinero recaudan, como muestran los antecedentes del mercado estadounidense, donde nueve de las diez IPO de al menos US$40 millones con mejores resultados en su primera jornada ocurrieron entre 1999 y 2000, durante el auge de las empresas de Internet”, explicó Felipe Oyarzún, analista de mercados de XTB. El especialista destacó que Newsmax pasó de un precio de colocación de US$10 por acción a cerrar su primera sesión en US$83,51, con una subida del 735,1%. Así, superó el histórico debut de VA Linux, cuyas acciones avanzaron un 697,5% en 1999. “Detrás de estas alzas suele haber una combinación de fuerte demanda y una cantidad limitada de acciones disponibles para negociar, lo que puede impulsar rápidamente los precios sin garantizar que esas ganancias se mantengan”, agregó. El analista también advirtió sobre la importancia de distinguir entre el precio de colocación de una OPI y el precio al que las acciones comienzan a negociarse en el mercado secundario. Esto significa que quienes compran durante la primera jornada no necesariamente obtienen toda la rentabilidad reflejada en las cifras del debut. El caso de Anthropic ilustra la diferencia entre el tamaño de una oferta pública inicial y el desempeño de las acciones. Aunque protagonizó la mayor OPI de la historia por monto recaudado, sus títulos cerraron su primera sesión con una subida del 17,1%, lejos de los avances registrados por las empresas que encabezan el ranking de XTB. De acuerdo con el informe de XTB, estas son las diez empresas que registraron las mayores alzas entre su precio de colocación y el cierre de su primera jornada bursátil: Se toman en cuenta solo OPI superiores a los US$40 millones. El desempeño posterior de estas compañías también evidencia los riesgos de las fuertes subidas iniciales. Según el análisis de XTB, ninguna consiguió sostener a largo plazo la valoración alcanzada al cierre de su primera jornada bursátil.

item.content:encoded:

World

COP31 climate talks collapse as EU and others reject deal

The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted by all parties was in Copenhagen in 2009.

COP31 President Murat Kurum speaks during the plenary session at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye on Nov 22, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Murad Sezer)

22 Nov 2026 10:38PM (Updated: 22 Nov 2026 10:56PM)

FAST

ANTALYA: United Nations climate talks collapsed on Sunday (Nov 22) as the European Union and others rejected a final draft deal put forward by COP31 presidents Türkiye and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming. The failed talks reflect world governments' struggle this year to muster ambitious action to address the worsening consequences of climate change, as wars, economic pressures and other crises compete for their attention. After more than two weeks of negotiations that spilt two days into overtime - making it the longest COP on record - Türkiye's conference president Murat Kurum said at the closing plenary that he could see there was no agreement and confirmed he would not advance any new text. "There is nothing to do, we did all that we could," he said. "There will be no new text from now on."

He later left the stage in the midst of speeches being delivered by country representatives. Australia's COP31 President of Negotiations, Chris Bowen, called the outcome "very disappointing" and said disagreements over fuels and climate finance were the dealbreakers. The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted by all parties was in Copenhagen in 2009. Ireland's environment minister Darragh O'Brien said the European Union could not support the proposed deal in part because it made no mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say drive global warming. "It is unconscionable that we would have a climate act that makes no reference to fossil fuel, no reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels," he said. Saudi Arabia and other big oil producer countries had lobbied hard to keep their mention out of the text, according to observers at the summit. Panama also said it could not support the text because it failed to address the scale and urgency of the climate crisis. This year's COP is the first since the UN's environmental body in October confirmed the rise in global temperature was set to exceed 1.5°C, a threshold countries agreed at Paris climate talks over a decade ago to try not to exceed, and beyond which extreme weather impacts intensify.

Related:

Fossil fuels still missing from latest COP31 draft deal

OPEC speaks up for fossil fuels at COP31 climate talks

Belgium's Climate Minister Jean-Luc Crucke said the failure of the deal was a difficult outcome, but appropriate. "It's not the end of multilateralism, but there has to be courage to say no," he said. While a blow to efforts to ratchet up international action, the failure to agree on a political declaration in Antalya does not erase the obligations agreed by previous UN conferences or remove the technical and legal frameworks governing multilateral action against climate change. PRESSURE FROM SAUDI ARABIA AND OTHER OIL PRODUCERS The failed deal had acknowledged the planet's projected temperature overshoot and called for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse it. That was a big ask from oil - producing countries. While scientists say removing carbon from the atmosphere - when paired with steep emissions cuts - is vital to avoiding the worst impacts of climate change, critics of the proposed deal said they worried the carbon removal language would be used as a licence to keep pumping oil. A representative for the Saudi delegation, which supported the deal's mention of carbon removal, told the summit at the closing plenary that he was surprised at the resistance to technology, which he said offered a concrete solution. Developing countries had also criticised the deal for not providing sufficient new climate finance to help them adapt to a warming planet. The deal had called for a tripling of such finance, but did not specify from what baseline. The failed deal had also included a goal put forward by Türkiye to expand electricity's share of total final world energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035, from around 23 per cent now. Proponents of that pledge said it could cut greenhouse gas emissions by speeding the transition away from fuel-powered cars, furnaces, and other equipment. But critics said it could force more costs onto poor nations without providing a clear path away from fossil fuels. The COP process is the main vehicle through which countries coordinate their efforts to curb global warming. Its annual meeting provides an opportunity for nations to signal they are willing to work together to find solutions and help finance the problems rising temperatures cause.

Source: Reuters/dc

FAST

MANCHESTER, England,, Nov 22 : Manchester City missed out on the chance to move into first place in the Women's Super League on Sunday, suffering a 3-1 defeat at home by Tottenham Hotspur that leaves them second in the standings.  With leaders Chelsea held to a 1-1 draw by Liverpool on Saturday, reigning champions City looked set to capitalise on that slip-up when they took a 1-0 lead thanks to a Bunny Shaw goal in the 10th minute. However, Norwegian striker Cathinka Tandberg levelled for Spurs just before the break.  City stuttered in attack, and they were punished in the 74th minute when Drew Spence sliced them open with a pass through the middle that Matilda Vinberg picked up before slotting into the net, and Jessica Naz added a goal on her 100th WSL appearance shortly afterwards to make it 3-1.  The defeat leaves City on 25 points after 11 games, two behind Chelsea and two ahead of third-placed London City Lionesses, while the win lifts Spurs to fifth on 20 points.  In the day's other early kick-off, Simi Awujo struck deep into second-half stoppage time to give Manchester United a 2-1 win away to Birmingham City to leave them fourth in the table on 21 points.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Nvidia Board Faces a Governance Reckoning
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg opinion columnist Gautam Mukunda tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has exposed broader corporate governance problems, as the board faces outside pressure to bring him back while investigations and potential shareholder litigation loom. Mukunda argues that Silicon Valley’s tendency to concentrate power around founder CEOs can weaken oversight, while Huang’s exit also complicates the debate over whether the US should allow advanced Nvidia chips to be sold to China. Nvidia has publicly said its board does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

FAST

GURGL, Austria, Nov 22 : Timon Haugan held off compatriot Eirik Hystad Solberg to win the men's World Cup slalom in Gurgl as Norway claimed the top two places on Sunday. Haugan clocked a combined time of one minute 42.55 seconds to finish 0.60 seconds ahead of Solberg, with Switzerland's Tanguy Nef completing the podium, 0.88 behind. "It's a huge relief," Haugan told Viaplay after claiming his seventh World Cup victory and becoming the first Norwegian to win a World Cup race at the Austrian venue. Gurgl joined the World Cup calendar in 2023. Haugan had endured a difficult build-up to the season after discovering he had used the wrong binding setup for much of his preparation.

"It's been one of the toughest pre-seasons I've had, with a lot of doubt and uncertainty. I thought I just had to go for it today. Better to do it now than later," he added. Solberg delivered a strong second run to secure the first World Cup podium of his career. "It doesn't get any more fun than that," Solberg said. Atle Lie McGrath, who trailed Haugan by just one hundredth of a second after the opening run, failed to finish his second descent. Fellow Norwegian Henrik Kristoffersen also went out in the deciding run. Brazil's Lucas Pinheiro Braathen saw his bid to win the opening three races of the season end when he straddled a gate early in the first run. He had won the giant slalom in Soelden and the slalom in Levi.

Source: Reuters

FAST

PORTIMAO, Nov 22 : Ducati's Marc Marquez sealed the 2026 MotoGP crown at the Portuguese Grand Prix on Sunday, his eighth-place finish enough to establish an unassailable lead in the standings and place him alongside the great Giacomo Agostini on eight premier-class titles. Marquez needed to finish in the top nine in Sunday's race and despite starting second on the grid, the Spaniard rode with caution to finish eighth and seal the title with a round to spare. The race was won by Marco Bezzecchi, who held a 102-point advantage over Marquez at one stage this season, while his Aprilia team mate Jorge Martin and Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez completed the podium. However, all eyes were on Marquez, who marked the occasion by scaling a scaffold to address the cheering fans before watching a big-screen montage of the defining moments of his career.

MARQUEZ, THE 'GOAT' As a final flourish, the Spaniard ascended a staircase accompanied by the silhouette of a goat on the screen, a nod to his growing 'Greatest of All Time' status, before receiving a golden commemorative helmet from Agostini himself. He then attached another plaque with his name engraved on it on the Tower of Champions before embracing and lifting it over his head. "We need to be happy. I know that we are here celebrating a historic moment. I know how I suffered," said an emotional Marquez, who underwent double surgery midway through the season. "I know that in the middle of the season, the fans believed more than I did. My people believed more than I did. But I kept pushing, I kept doing my best. "I said last year that it was a championship where I was at peace with myself. This one is for all the fans that believed in me from 2020 until now. So thanks to all of you, this is for all of you." Marquez came agonisingly close to securing the title in Saturday's sprint but his hopes were dashed when he crashed out on the penultimate lap while running in third place, a finish that would have been sufficient to crown him champion. But unlike Saturday's overcast conditions and spots of rain on the circuit, Sunday's 25-lap race was held in bright sunshine. TOP-NINE FINISH ENOUGH FOR MARQUEZ Martin needed to outscore Marquez by 18 points while the Ducati rider's equation was far more simple: secure a top-nine finish regardless of his rivals' results to get his hands on the trophy. Marquez had been cautious in the sprint but this time he shot off the line to take the lead from polesitter Bezzecchi while several riders jostled for position behind him, with Martin moving up from seventh to fourth. But Marquez was soon swallowed up by the faster Aprilia bikes around him, with the championship leader quickly falling to seventh as he exercised caution amid aggressive overtaking. A crash from Pedro Acosta moved Marquez up to sixth but he had to concede two places to Fabio Di Giannantonio and Ai Ogura, with the Ducati rider happy to open the door to let them pass knowing eighth would be good enough for the title. Up front, Bezzecchi finally moved past Fernandez to take the lead on lap 15 while Martin also found a way past three laps later with an identical overtake to make it a factory Aprilia one-two. On lap 19, Marquez fell to ninth as KTM's Brad Binder nudged him aside to overtake and there was concern from his legion of fans at the Algarve International Circuit, but a crash from Diogo Moreira on the last lap moved Marquez up to eighth. "Super happy about the season, obviously some highs and some lows, but my best season in MotoGP so far," said Bezzecchi, who missed races with his own injuries. "Still a lot of things to improve. But congrats to Marc, he really deserves everything. He's one of the strongest riders in history, so to fight with him is an honour. "Hopefully next year I will fight again and make his life even harder."

Source: Reuters

item.title: アンソロピックＩＰＯ、銀行に異例の制約 競合担当禁止や人数制限
item.description:
Echo Wang Milana Vinn
［ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター］ - 過去最大規模となった米人工知能（Ａ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アンソロピックＩＰＯ、銀行に異例の制約　競合担当禁止や人数制限 11/22 22:09 配信

ニューヨークのタイムズスクエアで19日撮影　REUTERS/Shannon Stapleton/File Photo（ロイター） Echo Wang　Milana Vinn

［ニューヨーク　２２日　ロイター］ - 過去最大規模となった米人工知能（ＡＩ）企業アンソロピックの新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）。引き受け銀行は巨額の報酬を得たが、ＩＰＯの過程でアンソロピックが異例なほどの制約を銀行側にかけていたことが関係者の話で分かった。アンソロピックと並ぶ大型上場を遂げたスペースＸでも同様な状況だったという。

６月のスペースＸのＩＰＯでは、数カ月にわたる手続きをスペースＸが厳しく管理し、財務などの情報を開示しなかった。このためアドバイザーは業務を進めにくく、銀行の担当者らは不満を募らせた。

社内で「プロジェクト・ランタン」と呼ばれたアンソロピックのＩＰＯでも、銀行側は振り回された。直前の変更や財務見通しの共有の遅れ、慌ただしい書類承認、銀行に対する極めて異例の制約などだ。

関係者によると、アンソロピックは２２社の引受金融機関の一部に対し、案件に携わる要員を４人までに絞り、上級職員を充てるよう指示した。また銀行の一部の幹部に、法的文書への署名を求めた。案件チームの中核メンバーが上場後６カ月間、オープンＡＩ、カーソル、ディープシーク、ハギング・フェイスなどの競合企業と仕事をすることを制限する内容だった。

銀行は日常的に利益相反を管理し、顧客の機密を守っている。ＩＰＯでこれほどの制限を求めるのはまれで、まして銀行担当者個々に求めることは異例という。

＜情報漏えいに神経とがらす＞

こうした銀行に対する制約は、一つに情報漏えいを防ぐことが目的だった。

アンソロピックが米証券取引委員会（ＳＥＣ）に提出した届出書「フォームＳ─１」が公開される４週間近く前に、ロイターはその内容を報じた。

アンソロピックは、案件を引き受けた大半の銀行との情報共有に、通常のＰＤＦではなく「ネットロードショー」と呼ばれるサービスを使った。

ネットロードショーは、誰が文書を閲覧し、どのページを見たかといったアクセスの詳細を記録する。ネットロードショー上の文書には、バンカー個人の名前が透かしとして入った。

その後もＩＰＯ書類に関する報道は続いた。関係者の１人によると、ネットロードショーの利用で銀行側の業務は煩雑になった。文書のコピーを保存できないことなどが理由だ。

アンソロピックは１０日に仮条件を記載した修正届出書「Ｓ─１Ａ」をＳＥＣに提出し、販売活動を始める予定だった。そのためには、シンジケート団の全銀行に草案を送り、承認を得る必要があるが、送付を巡って混乱があり、銀行側に届け出書がＳ─１Ａがネットロードショー経由で送られたのはニューヨーク時間午前２時ごろ。ＳＥＣへの提出に向け、銀行側に、承認のために与えられた時間は数時間しかなかったという。

銀行担当者からは「手続きが複雑な問題だらけで、これまで手掛けたどの案件とも違っていた」との声が出ている。

ＩＰＯを研究するフロリダ大学のジェイ・リッター名誉教授によると、スペースＸとアンソロピックはいずれも交渉により、グリーンシューオプション（追加売り出し）で売却する追加株式について、引受会社に手数料を一切支払わないことを取り付けた。「これらの企業には確かに、引受会社に対して『いつも通りにはいかない』と告げるだけの市場支配力があった」と指摘した。

アンソロピック、および両ＩＰＯで主幹事を務めたゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーはコメントを控えた。

スペースＸはコメント要請に応じなかった。

ロイター 関連リンク 焦点：人民元に内外の圧力、海外は割安批判　国内は元高懸念 焦点：オープンＡＩの甘いセキュリティー管理、従業員は以前から警鐘 コラム：安全資産性薄まる金　リスクオフでも買われず アングル：米ナスダック１００、10月に時価総額2兆ドル超消失　ＡＩ巨額投資に厳しい目 アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める 11/22(日) 22:09 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: Las profesiones más y menos confiables en 2026 en el mundo y América Latina, según informe de Ipsos
item.description: Los políticos, los influenciadores de redes sociales y los ejecutivos de publicidad figuran entre las profesiones que generan menos confianza en 31 países.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Salazar Castellanos
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — Los médicos encabezan la lista de las profesiones que generan mayor confianza entre la ciudadanía mundial, según el Índice de Confiabilidad Global de Ipsos 2026. A ellos les siguen los científicos y los profesores, de acuerdo con el estudio de la firma de investigación de mercados y consultoría, que encuestó a 23.537 adultos en 31 países. Ver más: Startups de América Latina captaron US$4.696 millones en 2025, el mayor monto desde 2022, según Endeavor Los médicos se mantienen como los profesionales más confiables desde 2024, según Ipsos. “En lo que respecta a la confianza, son más las cosas que unen a las personas de diferentes países que las que las dividen”, indica Ipsos. En todos los países, excepto en cuatro, “los médicos, los científicos y los profesores son las tres profesiones que gozan de mayor confianza”, indica la encuesta. En cambio, los políticos, los influenciadores de redes sociales y los ejecutivos de publicidad figuran entre las profesiones que generan menos confianza en 31 países. (Confianza neta). Fuente: Ipsos En Argentina, los doctores también son la profesión más confiable en 2026 con el 69% de las menciones, al igual que en México (64%). En Brasil, los profesores (56% de las menciones) son los profesionales más confiables, mientras en Colombia (56%) y Perú son los científicos (51%). En Chile, los menos confiables son los políticos (72%), el nivel más alto entre sus pares Argentina, Colombia y Perú (68%). También son los menos confiables en México (62%) y Brasil (66%), pero en menor proporción. En promedio, el 34% considera que la gente común de su país es digna de confianza. Los países de Asia Pacífico tienen mayor probabilidad de obtener puntuaciones de confianza más altas. Turquía, Hungría y Japón son los únicos países donde es más probable que se considere al ciudadano promedio poco confiable que confiable, de acuerdo con la encuesta de Ipsos. Ver más: Empleos remotos y globales: los perfiles latinos más demandados por la IA, según Alexander Torrenegra Ipsos informó que, por primera vez este año, consultaron a los ciudadanos si confiaban en los chatbots de IA. A esta pregunta, solo el 23% respondió que los considera fiables, mientras que el 40% opina que no lo son. En nueve países, la mayoría considera a los chatbots de IA. poco fiabless. “Todos estos países son de habla inglesa o están en Europa, lo que pone de manifiesto que el escepticismo hacia la IA es mayor en estos países”, dice. Otra de las novedades de este año es la inclusión de los directivos de empresas de inteligencia artificial y otros líderes de la industria tecnológica. En promedio, los emprendedores tecnológicos generan más confianza (31%) que desconfianza (25%). Ocupan el noveno lugar entre 22 profesiones evaluadas y reciben una mayor valoración de confianza que los líderes empresariales en general, que registran un 24%. Sin embargo, indica Ipsos, “cuando observamos el país donde tienen su sede muchos de los emprendedores tecnológicos más conocidos, vemos una historia diferente al promedio mundial. En Estados Unidos, solo el 22% los considera dignos de confianza, mientras que el 38% los considera poco confiables”. item.title: China's spies set sights on AI semiconductors years before Nvidia scandal
item.description: China's espionage agency has been running a secret campaign to help the country's companies acquire advanced AI chips and to gather intelligence on the sector, officials say ...
item.dc:creator: NYT
item.content:encoded: By Chris Buckley and Julian E Barnes When China’s top espionage agency updated its priorities this year, it added a revealing goal: overcoming Western barriers to technologies that Xi Jinping sees as crucial to China’s rise. At the heart of that quest are the advanced semiconductors needed to power artificial intelligence, including chips that the United States has barred US companies like Nvidia from exporting to China. China must “adopt extraordinary measures to intensify the drive for core technologies in priority sectors,” Xi told the Politburo, a council of senior officials, in January, according to an official text of his speech. “As swiftly as possible, solve the ‘chokehold’ problems holding back development of future industries.” The spy agency, the Ministry of State Security, has long been dedicated to eliminating threats to Communist Party rule in China. Now, it has made it a priority to acquire advanced semiconductor chips and gather intelligence about them, according to several serving and former security and intelligence officials from governments outside China in Asia, the United States and Europe. How China’s spy agency is seeking to obtain advanced chips and intelligence about them has become a central question in the case of Alice Huang. She is a Chinese businesswoman whom US officials say the Chinese agency was working with to spy on Jensen Huang, the chief executive of the American chip giant Nvidia, allegations that were first reported by The New York Times. Huang has not responded to requests for comment, and China has rejected the claims of espionage as “pure fabrication.” The Chinese spy agency’s campaign to acquire chips, details of which have not been previously reported, has been underway for at least two years, according to the current and former officials. They spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive intelligence. Among the campaign’s main elements: - The head of the spy agency, Chen Yixin, who holds the title of minister of state security, created a working team that is leading the effort and reports directly to him, multiple foreign officials said. Chen has worked under Xi since they were officials in Zhejiang Province in eastern China, a cradle of China’s high-tech boom.- The group was assigned to help China’s “counter-blockade” work — efforts to overcome export controls imposed by the United States and its allies.- The campaign includes helping Chinese companies acquire and smuggle advanced chips into China.- The group also collects intelligence about the semiconductor sector and its supply chains, according to several officials briefed on the campaign.In April, Chen unveiled the new mission. “Deepen the struggle against blockades, and comprehensively advance artificial intelligence innovation, industry development, and applications,” Chen wrote in a Communist Party journal. “Focus on tackling the ‘chokeholds’ of critical technologies,” he wrote, and solve the problem of technologies that “cannot be obtained by asking, buying or pleading.” “Chen is signalling to the party leadership and his own ranks that his agency is elevating AI competition with the US as a long-term, top priority,” said Alex Joske, the managing director of security practice at Garnaut Global, a consultancy firm, who studies the Chinese security apparatus. “He is telling his officers to find more ways to wage this struggle.” A Central Strategy The ministry’s campaign is part of a wider push by the ruling Communist Party to overcome Western-imposed restrictions on critical technology. China is determined to close its gap with the United States in the computing capacity needed for progress in artificial intelligence. At the top, that effort is being coordinated by the Central Science and Technology Commission. The commission is a secretive Communist Party organ that Xi established in 2023. This was not long after the US Commerce Department, in late 2022, started banning exports of Nvidia’s advanced chips directly to China, out of concern that the chips could help Beijing crack American encryption and design new weapons. The party commission is ranked higher than ministries and is led by Ding Xuexiang, one of only seven members of the Communist Party’s Politburo Standing Committee, its inner circle of power. “Computing power is a major indicator of overall national power,” Ding said in May when he visited energy and computing facilities in Beijing and nearby regions that are part of a planned nationwide AI computing network, according to Xinhua, China’s official news agency. Xi created the commission to better marshal the country’s scientists, institutes, labs across ministries and companies for national priorities such as achieving technological self-reliance. The commission rarely surfaces in Chinese news reports; its budgets and plans are not made public. But it has become an engine of Xi’s plans for technological pre-eminence, said Christopher K Johnson, a former Central Intelligence Agency analyst focused on China. The director of the commission, Ding, has long been a close aide to Xi and is also a vice-premier overseeing science and technology policy. The Spy Agency’s ‘Anti-Blockade Struggle’ China’s espionage service and other parts of the government have for decades pursued technology and research from abroad, using both open and illicit methods. But under Xi, that effort assumed greater urgency, with more top-level coordination, including in artificial intelligence, several experts said. Throughout this year, Chen, the agency’s chief, has repeatedly said the “anti-blockade struggle” is one of the key duties of China’s Ministry of State Security. “Certain countries are going to every length to impose a ‘chokehold’ on China in fields of critical technology,” Chen wrote in a party journal last year. “Technology competition among the major powers has entered its most intense, most strenuous and most critical phase of close-quarters combat.” As American companies, followed by Chinese ones, developed successively powerful AI models, officials in Beijing have increasingly recognised the potential for artificial intelligence to threaten their power at home and abroad, said Gregory C Allen, the founder and chief executive of Decision Tree Research, a firm that specialises in AI and other advanced technologies. In September, Chen himself referred to US tech companies and their AI models — like Claude Mythos and GPT-5.5-Cyber — as examples of new cybersecurity threats, as he described the risks that AI posed to the party’s hold on power. “China’s senior leadership understands that AI is critically, strategically essential, and that leadership in AI is obviously related to leadership in semiconductors,” said Allen, a former senior official at the US Department of Defense’s Joint Artificial Intelligence Center. Chen became the state security minister in late 2022, and just over a year later, the ministry issued a warning that AI was “highly likely in the near future to profoundly transform the national security landscape.” In 2024, the ministry said that its officers were scoring successes against the attempts of “the United States and other Western countries to lock us in at the low-end” of technology. The Role of Businesses and Other Groups China has sometimes used front organisations or researchers to collect information about foreign AI technology, said Joske, the consultant. “M.S.S. is very comfortable using business covers,” he said, “and it’s very comfortable running people as assets without directly telling those people that they’re working for the M.S.S.” Such covers could include organisations ostensibly focused on academic research. In September, MI5, the British security agency, asserted that a Chinese research institute linked to the Chinese spy agency had drawn in British scientists for research that, apparently unbeknown to the scientists, “directly improves M.S.S. technical capability for espionage.” Companies such as the one Alice Huang founded, Megaspeed, are viewed as another potential vehicle for gathering intelligence. The precise nature of Alice Huang’s role in the ministry’s chip effort remains unclear. US officials say Huang, who was having an affair with the Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, passed information to Beijing about him. The US government is also investigating Megaspeed for illegally smuggling advanced chips into China. Megaspeed, which is based in Singapore, bought billions of dollars of Nvidia chips and entered the business of providing high-end computing capacity to Chinese companies. Such services have allowed Chinese businesses to use Nvidia chips at data centres abroad by sidestepping US rules that ban sales of the most advanced AI chips directly to Chinese firms. Last week, The Times also reported that Megaspeed was possibly aiding a lab with links to China’s military, through Alibaba, the Chinese internet giant. Alibaba is a customer and financial backer of Megaspeed. Providing Nvidia chips to support research for China’s military would be a violation of US law. An Alibaba spokeswoman said: “Any suggestions that Alibaba provides services to the military is groundless. Alibaba Cloud’s service agreement strictly prohibits the use of our products and services for any military purpose.” In an effort to address what many in Washington see as a loophole, the Trump administration announced on Monday that it would move ahead with a new rule to prevent China from being able to access advanced semiconductors from Nvidia and other US companies through the use of data centres outside China. The new restriction will require overseas data centres to obtain a government licence before supplying “significant volumes of computing power” to firms with headquarters in countries on a list that includes China, Russia and Iran. It goes into effect in about 90 days. The restriction could make China’s pursuit of self-reliance more urgent, a goal Xi has cast as a fight for survival, echoing the party’s revolutionary past. “Like the Red Army on the Long March, we’re now on a new Long March,” he told technicians while visiting an AI data hub under construction in northern China last month. He was referring to a gruelling trek taken by Communist troops in the 1930s that cemented Mao’s leadership of the revolution. “You are an army in the drive for advanced technological self-reliance.”

FAST

Nov 22 : Paris St Germain forward Desire Doue will undergo surgery later this month after suffering a serious right knee injury, the Ligue 1 champions said on Sunday, with no timeline yet set for his return. The 21-year-old France international was carried off in tears towards the end of the first half of PSG's 3-2 victory at Nice on Saturday after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee. Doue had earlier scored his second league goal of the season, but was injured when his fully extended leg buckled as he turned to shield the ball from Nice midfielder Sofiane Diop, with no contact between the players. The injury is the latest setback for Doue, who missed parts of last season with calf and hamstring problems.

item.title: ＣＯＰ３１が合意採択断念、ＥＵなど反対 化石燃料巡り対立
item.description:
Sarah McFarlane Peter Hobson
［アンタルヤ（トルコ） ２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Sarah McFarlane　Peter Hobson

［アンタルヤ（トルコ） ２２日　ロイター］ - トルコのアンタルヤで開催されていた国連気候変動枠組み条約第３１回締約国会議（ＣＯＰ３１）は会期延長２日目となる２２日、共同議長国のトルコとオーストラリアが合意文書の新たな草案を公表したが、欧州連合（ＥＵ）などが反対し、採択を断念した。

議長を務めるトルコのムラト・クルム環境・都市計画・気候変動相は、閉会の全体会合で、「本文書についてコンセンサス（合意）がないことを認める。従って、これらの決定は採択されなかった」と述べた。「今後、新たな文書は出さない」とも述べた。

前回、合意採択が見送られたのは、２００９年にデンマークで開かれたＣＯＰ１５だ。「コペンハーゲン合意」を全会一致で採択できず、多国間の気候外交にとって打撃となった。

２０２６年下半期のＥＵ議長国アイルランドのダラ・オブライエン環境相は、科学者が地球温暖化の原因と指摘する化石燃料に全く触れていないことなどを理由にＥＵとして合意草案を支持できないと表明した。パナマも、気候危機の規模と緊急性に応えていないとして、草案を支持できないとした。

交渉を主導したオーストラリアと開催国トルコは、合意文書の草案を複数回示し、気候変動の影響を最も受けやすい国々と、化石燃料の生産や消費に経済を頼る国々の間で妥協点を探った。

２２日に示された最終草案は、気候変動対策の国際枠組み「パリ協定」が目指す産業革命前からの世界の気温上昇を１．５度に抑えるとの目標を超える軌道にあることを、初めて認めた上で、上限を超えた分を最終的に元に戻すため、二酸化炭素（ＣＯ２）除去技術の開発を急ぐよう求めていた。焦点となっていた気候変動の原因とされる化石燃料からの脱却には直接には触れず、その代わり、脱却を進めるとした過去の合意文書に言及した。

関係者の話では、サウジアラビアやその他の主要産油国が、文書に化石燃料の記載は入れず、炭素除去技術を盛り込むよう強く働きかけたという。一方、草案は野心に欠けるという批判が出た。

議長国は、各国が異議を申し立てるための時間を数時間設け、２２日中に全体会合を開き採択を目指していたが、意見の隔たりは埋まらなかった。

FAST

Nov 22 : South Africa have made two changes to their starting XI for the second and final test against Bangladesh in Centurion on Monday, with batter Tony de Zorzi and fast bowler Anrich Nortje included as the home side seek to win the series. Stand-in captain Aiden Markram confirmed the team on Sunday with De Zorzi included in place of regular skipper Temba Bavuma, who has a calf injury. Nortje comes into the side for Dane Paterson. South Africa won the first test by nine wickets, strengthening their position at the top of the World Test Championship table as they look to defend the title they claimed against Australia at Lord’s last year.   Markram said the wicket looks as though it will have pace and bounce as the game goes on.

"This looks like a pretty typical Centurion wicket," he said. "Generally, it can start off on the slower side and it just quickens up throughout the game. "It's known for a bit of pace and bounce, but also known as a venue where you can score big runs if you get in." Markram has stood in for Bavuma before and said the way the team operates will make it easy for him to do so again. "We've worked really well, to be honest," he said. "Temba is still going to be around this week, so I think it's quite a smooth transition, if there even is a transition. "Shuks (coach Shukri Conrad) is obviously really strong in his ways as well, and from my point of view, it's just about trying to carry those good things forward and trying to get a pulse of the game as quickly as you can, assessing conditions as quickly as you can and coming up with plans from there." Bangladesh scored 400 in their first innings at The Wanderers and took the test to the fifth day. Markram praised their application and expects more of the same at Centurion. "They batted well. They made 400 in the first innings, and first-innings runs, especially of that amount, will keep you in the game for quite a long period of time," he said.

item.title: Why Harsh Goenka calls Mexico President Claudia Sheinbaum's economy-class flight ‘a leadership lesson’
item.description: Harsh Goenka has praised Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum for reportedly travelling to China in economy class and using an ordinary airport shuttle. Her journey to the APEC summit has drawn attention to her leadership style, political career and decision to sell its presidential aircraft.
item.dc:creator: Anjali Thakur
item.content:encoded: Industrialist Harsh Goenka has praised Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum for travelling to China in economy class for the APEC summit, describing her journey as a lesson in leadership and public accountability.In a post on X, Goenka highlighted Sheinbaum's reported 21-hour journey, during which she travelled in a middle seat in economy class and used an ordinary airport shuttle after arriving in China.“A lesson in leadership from Mexico for the world: President Claudia Sheinbaum flew 21 hours to China in economy class, and that too the middle seat, and took an ordinary airport shuttle to the APEC summit. Mexico had earlier sold its $200 million luxury presidential aircraft, with the proceeds directed towards public priorities like hospitals. A powerful reminder that public office is a responsibility, not a licence for privilege.” The journey has attracted attention in China as well, with a hashtag related to her arrival reportedly receiving 10 million views on the Chinese social media platform Weibo.According to Bloomberg, a Weibo user posting under the handle Signal and Noise 001 said fellow passengers on a Mexico City-Shenzhen flight operated by China Southern Airlines had confirmed that Sheinbaum was seated in 33B, an economy-class seat towards the rear of the aircraft.A Mexican diplomat familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that the president travelled in economy class on the China Southern Airlines flight from Mexico City. The aircraft made a technical stopover in Tijuana, with the total journey taking around 21 hours.Footage shared on Sheinbaum's X account showed her being welcomed at Shenzhen airport by a military guard and a dancing troupe dressed in pink. She was seen arriving on an airport bus rather than being greeted as she stepped off an aircraft.Who is Claudia Sheinbaum?Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo is an environmental engineer and politician who has served as Mexico's president since 2024. She is the first woman and the first Jewish person to be elected to the country's highest political office.Born on June 24, 1962, in Mexico City, Sheinbaum studied physics at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), graduating in 1989. She subsequently earned a master's degree in 1994 and a PhD in energy engineering in 1995 from the same university.She was a faculty member and researcher at UNAM's Institute of Engineering from 1995 to 2000 and again from 2006 to 2015. During her academic career, she authored more than 100 articles and two books on energy, the environment and sustainable development.Sheinbaum was also a member of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). In 2007, the IPCC and former US vice president Al Gore jointly received the Nobel Peace Prize for “their efforts to build up and disseminate greater knowledge about man-made climate change, and to lay the foundations for the measures that are needed to counteract such change.”Sheinbaum's political career and Mexico's presidential aircraftBefore becoming president, Sheinbaum held several political and administrative positions. She served as secretary of the environment of Mexico City from 2000 to 2006, head of the Tlalpan delegation from 2015 to 2017, and head of government of Mexico City from 2018 to 2023.Her predecessor and political mentor, Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, sold Mexico's presidential aircraft in 2023 to the government of Tajikistan. The sale followed his decision to put the aircraft up for sale after taking office in 2018. Bloomberg reported that the former president, who rarely travelled outside Mexico and was critical of foreign summits, sold the aircraft at a loss to the government.China visit comes amid trade tensionsSheinbaum's warm reception in China comes against the backdrop of tensions over Mexico's trade policy. Her government has embraced higher duties on a range of Chinese imports, drawing a sharp rebuke from Beijing. The move also came as US President Donald Trump pressured countries in the Americas under his so-called Donroe Doctrine to assert US dominance over the Western Hemisphere.After a brief meeting with Trump in Shenzhen, Sheinbaum told reporters that Mexico and the US were close to reaching a trade agreement that negotiators had long struggled to finalise.“In business circles, Mexico is seen as being pressured into taking decisions that are against China,” said Alfredo Montufar-Helu, managing director for Ankura China Advisors based in Beijing. “Even so, Sheinbaum is well received in China.”Montufar-Helu, who is originally from Mexico, said Sheinbaum's popularity reflected growing awareness of Mexico in China, including interest in Mexican food and cultural celebrations such as the Day of the Dead. The festival gained popularity in China following the 2017 release of Pixar's animated film Coco, about a young Mexican boy who accidentally enters the Land of the Dead.Sheinbaum meets China's Xi JinpingSheinbaum met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Tuesday. The two Group of 20 leaders discussed strengthening trade ties and increasing Mexican exports to China.She described the meeting as “very cordial” and said the two countries discussed cooperation in areas including trains, vehicles, agriculture, tourism and health.

item.content:encoded:
News / U.Today / Hoskinson Weighs In on Cardano (ADA) Price Collapse

Hoskinson Weighs In on Cardano (ADA) Price Collapse 2 min read

ADAUSD ADAUSD Charles Hoskinson, founder of Cardano ADAUSD , has tried to clear the air regarding the utility of the cryptocurrency. This comes as ADA has fallen more than 95% from its all-time high. Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson responded to frustrated Cardano community members who are disappointed by the blockchain’s pace of development and inability to rebound from the current slump. Cardano utility vs. ADA price On Nov. 21, Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson took to X to counter criticism about the current state of Cardano. The exchange was triggered by a joke made by an X user stating that Grand Theft Auto 6 came out before a working Cardano blockchain. Hoskinson replied to the comment, saying: “Cardano works.” Later, Hoskinson addressed the poor price performance of the cryptocurrency and explained that price doesn’t always reflect the capabilities of blockchain networks. “Yeah. Price doesn't equal utility. Is Solana 75 percent less capable than it's all time high? It's an infinitely better product today for many more people. And so it is for Cardano,” he said. What this means is that even if the value of a blockchain network's native cryptocurrency is dropping, the technology can still advance. An X user, however, contested his comparison with Solana, stating that Cardano hasn’t been able to retake its previous all-time high even after years of development. This drew an increasingly irritated response from Hoskinson. “So every single thing a f****** scam? Everything they do failed? I’m so tired of you people,” said the Cardano founder. Cardano ADAUSD down 95% from all-time high This recent statement by Hoskinson comes as Cardano ADAUSD remains one of the worst-performing major cryptocurrencies in the current market downturn. As per CoinGlass data, ADA is currently trading at around $0.14. The cryptocurrency is down by about 57% since the beginning of 2026. It has lost a whopping 95.4% of its value from its all-time high of $3.09, set in September 2021. On Nov. 21, ADA briefly dipped toward $0.13. This came as another sell-off hit the broader crypto market. Cardano has been in a steady decline, leading to criticism regarding its adoption, activity in its ecosystem and ability to compete with the likes of Ethereum and Solana. Nonetheless, Charles Hoskinson has maintained that short-term market performance should not be conflated with the progress of blockchain technology over the long run. Earlier this month, the Cardano founder tried to reassure frustrated ADA holders and tell them that things would eventually get better. “It's all going to be ok. Everyone will be happy next year after all this madness, hate and idiocy,” said Hoskinson in a previous X post.

Schumer led Democrats to big Senate win. Now, some say they need a new leader

Reuters

22 November, 2026 05:00 pm IST

By Nolan D. McCaskill WASHINGTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) – Chuck Schumer led Senate Democrats through November’s midterm elections that gave them a decisive 56-seat majority. Progressives responded with a collective “thank you, next,” arguing he should now make way for a successor.

Critics say Schumer’s decades in Washington, his age and his close ties to the party establishment make him ill-suited to lead a caucus increasingly shaped by younger, anti-establishment lawmakers.

“We write first to thank you,” leaders of the populist Working Families Party, which backs like-minded Democratic candidates in elections, said in a November 13 letter to Schumer that called for a generational leadership change.

Show Full Article

“If you step aside at the height of a victory you helped secure, you would show voters that the Democratic Party heeded their call for change. The new majority can begin its work united and focused on fighting for the people who elected them.”

The top Democrat in the Senate for the past decade, Schumer, who turns 76 on Monday, has projected confidence that his colleagues will choose to keep him as their leader in a secret vote on December 1.

“I will be elected majority leader,” Schumer, who is strongly favored to win, told reporters matter-of-factly last week.

But in the first contested Senate Democratic leadership race since 1994, the New York senator faces a challenge from Senator Chris Van Hollen, 67. While only modestly younger than Schumer, the Maryland lawmaker and his progressive allies outside the Capitol have cast him as an agent of change.

Van Hollen has said the 2026 results show voters are demanding the party break with the status quo and adopt a bolder approach that gives new voices, including incoming progressive lawmakers, more influence in the caucus.

‘TIME FOR NEW IDEAS’

The Maryland Democrat has run an increasingly public campaign, though the outcome will be determined in private by 56 Senate Democrats. At least 16 Democrats have publicly committed to backing Schumer, while only six have said they will vote for Van Hollen.

“I’m in this to win it,” Van Hollen said on Thursday. “That’s my goal. I think if we want to move forward on an ambitious agenda like this, we need new leadership. We need to change the culture of the Democratic caucus. People need to have more input. Our new members need to be at the table.”

Democrats flipped nine Senate seats in November, including in several states President Donald Trump won by double digits in 2024. Many of the incoming freshmen said during their campaigns that they would oppose Schumer for Democratic leader.

“Do I like Chuck Schumer?” asked Senator-elect Troy Jackson of Maine. “He’s been great, but I do think it’s time for new ideas.”

In an interview last week on CNN’s “State of the Union,” Van Hollen cited a “hunger for change” among Senate Democrats and said two incoming senators won despite Schumer’s efforts to back their primary opponents. He criticized Schumer for aligning with powerful pro-Israel and cryptocurrency interests in those races.

PROGRESSIVES BACK VAN HOLLEN

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan said Van Hollen stands out because he understands how Washington and the Senate work as a past chair of House and Senate Democrats’ respective campaign arms, and he’s willing to take risks.

“Those two things are what we need right now, and we need to rethink the way we legislate,” he said, pointing to Van Hollen’s trips to advocate for a wrongly deported migrant and to draw attention to Israel’s war in Gaza as examples of his willingness to take risks.

Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia suggested the leadership fight reflected a healthy discussion within the caucus about its future direction. “And there’s nothing wrong with that,” he told Reuters.

Senate Democratic leader is the only unresolved role among Congress’ top four positions. House Democrats last week nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be speaker in the next Congress, where John Thune will continue to lead Senate Republicans and Representative Jim Jordan will succeed Speaker Mike Johnson as the top House Republican.

SCHUMER COULD FACE PRIMARY CHALLENGER IN 2028

Schumer is up for reelection in 2028, and losing the leadership race could make him a more vulnerable target, as ambitious Democrats such as Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez consider running for his seat. A memo from Ocasio-Cortez’s campaign acknowledged she could run for president, Senate or reelection to the House in 2028.

For his part, Schumer has swatted down questions about his future beyond the leadership election.

“I’m focused on 2027 and delivering for the American people,” he said on Wednesday.

(Reporting by Nolan D. McCaskill; Editing by Michael Learmonth and Cynthia Osterman)

Deal or no deal? COP31 climate talks lurch towards an uncertain finish

By Sarah McFarlane and Peter Hobson ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 22 (Reuters) – Two days after the official close of UN climate talks, COP31 presidents Australia and Turkey struggled to win consensus for a deal to advance the fight against climate change, raising the prospect of no deal being reached.

A new draft deal released on Sunday has yet to be approved as countries disagreed over issues including whether the accord should mention the fossil fuels scientists say are driving warming.

“While no one obtained everything they might have desired, everyone can find a place for themselves within this text. That is the very essence of consensus,” COP31 President Murat Kurum told the talks. “I hope that the decision emerging from this hall will demonstrate to the world that multilateralism is still capable of yielding results.”

Show Full Article

If approved, the current deal would acknowledge for the first time that global warming is on course to exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius (2.7-degree Fahrenheit) threshold that countries had sought to preserve, while calling for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse the overshoot.

Ireland’s environment minister Darragh O’Brien said the European Union could not support the proposed deal.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach,” he said.

Panama also said it could not support the current text.

DRAFT OMITS MENTION OF FOSSIL FUELS

The current draft omits mention of fossil fuels and instead includes language referring to a previous COP at which governments agreed to transition away from oil, gas, and coal.

Observers at the venue, where catering outlets and exhibits have already been dismantled, said Saudi Arabia and other big oil-producing nations had pushed hard in negotiations for keeping explicit mention of fossil fuels out of the text, and carbon removal in.

“It seems like we are negotiating with the Saudis,” said Tuvalu’s climate minister, Maina Talia.

A representative for the Saudi delegation declined to comment.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, several delegations raised the prospect of leaving without a deal.

Others said they worried that too many delegations had already left to catch their planes home, making it possible there would not be a quorum for a decision.

“We hope, of course, that we will still reach a decision. But given the last few hours, I’m sceptical that this can still succeed in the short time left, especially since many colleagues have already left,” said Carsten Schneider, Germany’s environment minister.

Jennifer Morgan, former German climate envoy and a senior fellow at The Fletcher School at Tufts University, said: “After the presidency ignored the views of 150 countries and tabled a very weak text, negotiations are on the brink.”

FOSSIL FUELS STICKING POINT

Environmental group 350.org said it was disappointed by the draft’s failure to mention fossil fuels explicitly, as well as its encouragement of carbon-removal technologies.

“Carbon capture is one of the biggest scams of the overshoot era, and our leaders are on the verge of falling for it,” said Sara Shaw, the group’s campaigns and networks director, referring to the practice of trapping carbon dioxide before it reaches the atmosphere.

Critics say the technologies are expensive and unproven at scale, and that including them in a deal is likely to spur continued oil and gas development.

The new draft text followed intensive consultations between Australia, which is leading the talks, Turkey, which is hosting the meeting, and delegations from nearly 200 countries.

The presidency gave delegations several hours to raise any objections to the deal, with a session scheduled later on Sunday to begin approving it.

Australia’s task, supported by Turkey, has been to find a deal that balances the needs of nations most vulnerable to climate change with those whose economies depend on either the production or consumption of fossil fuels.

This year’s COP is the first since the UN’s environmental body confirmed that the rise in global temperature was set to exceed 1.5C, a threshold all countries agreed over a decade ago to try not to exceed, and beyond which extreme weather impacts intensify.

(Reporting by Ali Kucukgocmen, Tuvan Gumrukcu, Ezgi Erkoyun, Sarah McFarlane, Valerie Volcovici, Lewis Jackson, Simon Jessop and Peter Hobson; Writing by William James and Richard Valdmanis; Editing by William Mallard and Barbara Lewis)

Exclusive-Like SpaceX, Anthropic ran an unusual IPO process, chafing some bankers

FILE PHOTO: An Anthropic, PBC (ANT) sign in Times Square on the day Anthropic held its initial public offering (IPO) at the NASDAQ Market site in New York City, US, November 19, 2026. REUTERS/Shannon Stapleton/File Photo

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 22 : For the second time this year, Wall Street bankers and lawyers took home a massive paycheck from a record-setting initial public offering. And for the second time this year, some of them came out of it complaining in private about how the process was riddled with complications and unlike any they had worked on before. With SpaceX’s IPO in June, in which banks earned half a billion dollars in fees, bankers chafed over how tightly the Elon Musk-led company controlled the months-long process and kept financial and other information private, making it hard for advisers to do their jobs.  As Anthropic’s IPO, dubbed internally “Project Lantern”, eclipsed SpaceX on Thursday and bankers took home more than half a billion dollars in fees, several people close to the process listed a litany of problems that had plagued the offering process: a compressed timeline, marred by last-minute changes and delays in sharing financial projections; rushed document approvals; and highly unusual restrictions on bankers and concern about leaks — especially after Reuters reported many details from a draft IPO filing weeks before it was made public. Anthropic, for example, instructed some of its 22 IPO underwriters to limit the number of bankers working on the deal to four, asking the firms to make sure they were senior staff, several people familiar with the matter said. One of the people said the restriction likely came out of fear that information would leak, and that the banks found a way to work around it anyway.

Underlying these complaints is a new power dynamic between technology companies and Wall Street. Companies such as SpaceX, Anthropic — and potentially also OpenAI in the future —  have come to wield enormous power as the transformative potential of artificial intelligence creates a frenzied demand for their shares, and they are wielding it to do things their way. That is upsetting some bankers. But banks and investors appear to have little choice but to play along. “These companies certainly did have some market power to tell underwriters that it’s not going to be business as usual,” said Jay Ritter, a University of Florida professor emeritus who researches IPOs. “But the big Wall Street firms, I suspect, are still going to be doing things as business as usual for all but maybe OpenAI (after these two deals).” Ritter added that both SpaceX and Anthropic had negotiated to pay underwriters nothing on the additional shares sold through the greenshoe option. “I don't think most companies are going to be able to demand zero spread on overallotment shares,” he said. Anthropic, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, the two lead underwriters on the two IPOs, declined to comment. SpaceX and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment. Both SpaceX and Anthropic debuted successfully, raising record amounts of money, and their shares rallied initially. A key part of the underwriters’ job is to market the securities. Thanks to the demand for AI, that was an easy sell — both companies had order books oversubscribed many times over.  After an initial burst in shares, the trajectories of the two big AI firms diverged. SpaceX climbed to a post-listing peak of $201.80 on June 16 before retreating below its $135 IPO price for the first time in mid-July. Anthropic’s shares closed down 8.5 per cent on Friday after a 17 per cent first-day pop, as a dramatic unraveling of the AI trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector. UNUSUAL NON-COMPETES AND RESTRICTIONS In the case of SpaceX’s IPO, the people close to the process said Musk’s team dictated terms at every stage. Musk's team told the largest and most powerful US banks — including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley — how to market SpaceX's stock and to whom. It told some banks the specific order sizes they needed to “fill” — in some cases a few billion dollars — and gave them instructions on what types of investors to bring. Banks signed on to underwrite the IPO without being told what they would be paid, the people said. The underlying current running through Anthropic’s IPO process was what several of the people who spoke to Reuters interpreted as a sense of extreme caution.     Anthropic asked some senior officers at banks working on its IPO to sign legal documents restricting core members of the transaction team from working with rival companies, including OpenAI, Cursor, DeepSeek and Hugging Face, for six months after it went public, according to the people.  Banks routinely manage conflicts and protect client confidentiality. But bankers and lawyers said it is rare for an IPO to impose exclusivity this broad, particularly on individual bankers.  In previous head-to-head IPOs such as those of ridesharing rivals Uber and Lyft, or real estate companies Trulia and Zillow, banks could simply pick a side, in part because the deals were smaller and required fewer banks.  Anthropic, by contrast, needed a broad syndicate to raise the enormous amount of capital it was seeking. That, some of the people said, explained why Anthropic sought to bind individual bankers with these restrictions.  One banker who declined to sign on to the agreement said it was a challenge to find people who could promise not to actively cover or engage with Anthropic’s peers, especially as several of those companies pursue their own initial or secondary offerings.   INFORMATION LEAKS AND LATE NIGHTS  Some of the restrictions were meant to control leaks of information.  Nearly four weeks before Anthropic’s filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, called Form S-1, was made public, Reuters reported on it, revealing details of the company’s financials, risk factors, dealings with other tech companies and other information.  Anthropic also used a product called NetRoadshow to share information, instead of regular PDFs, with most of the banks underwriting the deal.  NetRoadshow logs access details, including information such as who has seen the document and looked at which page. Documents on NetRoadshow also had individual bankers’ names as watermarks.  Leaks continued to surface in the press, but using NetRoadshow complicated bankers' work, including because the platform would not let them save copies of documents, one of the people said. Anthropic planned to file an updated securities filing, called an S-1A, with the SEC with the price range and to launch the marketing on November 10. To do so, it needed to send a draft to all the banks in its syndicate for them to sign off on it. The night before it was to happen, a law firm on the deal sent a PDF to the banks about the sale of shares in Canada. But soon it followed with another email asking them to disregard it, saying it “contains incorrect price range and share information,” according to the email, which was seen by Reuters.   The correct S-1A was then sent via the NetRoadshow platform around 2 a.m. New York time. Banks were told they had several hours to sign off on it before it was filed with the SEC.

item.title: Los viejos intermediarios del petróleo venezolano siguen bajo la lupa tras la caída de Maduro
item.description: Aunque la estructura de comercialización ha incorporado nuevos participantes, Transparencia Venezuela advierte que figuras vinculadas a las redes anteriores siguen presentes.
item.dc:creator: Raylí Luján
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — La captura de Nicolás Maduro no ha despejado las interrogantes sobre quiénes controlan el negocio petrolero venezolano ni sobre el destino de sus ingresos. Aunque la estructura de comercialización ha incorporado nuevos participantes y algunos operadores han salido del sector, Transparencia Venezuela advierte que figuras vinculadas a las redes anteriores siguen presentes. La organización también cuestiona las condiciones en que se están asignando los campos petroleros y la falta de información sobre los beneficiarios finales de las empresas que participan en el sector. Ver más: Exportaciones de petróleo venezolano caen a su nivel más bajo en ocho meses por alza en el precio de fletes Transparencia Venezuela entregó esta semana a la Fiscalía Federal del Distrito Sur de Nueva York un informe que busca aportar elementos a la investigación penal que se sigue contra Maduro y Cilia Flores en esa jurisdicción. El documento reconstruye el papel del exmandatario dentro de una red de corrupción transnacional y sus conexiones con economías ilícitas, a partir de diez años de registros, expedientes judiciales, decisiones administrativas y bases de datos. El informe, titulado Corrupción, captura del Estado y redes transnacionales en Venezuela , reconstruye una estructura de 13.521 actores, 30.467 relaciones y 865 empresas, vinculada a 154 casos de corrupción. Según el análisis de la ONG, Maduro ocupa el primer lugar en intermediación estructural dentro de esa red, un indicador que mide su posición como conexión entre distintos actores. En 96 de los 154 casos documentados desde 2013, Transparencia Venezuela identificó US$36.115 millones comprometidos. Para los otros expedientes, el monto no ha sido determinado o publicado. El informe también registra 110 casos que llegaron a tribunales de 26 países y 651 personas vinculadas a las investigaciones: 413 banqueros, empresarios e intermediarios y 238 funcionarios de organismos públicos y del sistema de justicia. La entrega del expediente busca contribuir a las pesquisas de las autoridades estadounidenses. De Freitas ha explicado que la documentación acumulada por la organización durante años permite reconstruir relaciones entre funcionarios, intermediarios, empresas y estructuras financieras. La directora de Transparencia Venezuela también ha señalado las dificultades que supone investigar estas tramas desde otros países. En su experiencia de colaboración con fiscales y cuerpos policiales extranjeros, uno de los obstáculos ha sido explicar el contexto económico e institucional venezolano. Los mecanismos de control cambiario, las diferencias entre las tasas oficiales y las del mercado y las conversiones de bolívares a dólares forman parte de operaciones que no siempre resultan sencillas de reconstruir desde otros sistemas financieros. A ello se suma la necesidad de entender cómo las decisiones administrativas y los controles estatales facilitaron determinadas transacciones. La dimensión de esas redes también aparece en una investigación anterior de Transparencia Venezuela sobre el circuito de comercialización petrolera entre 2019 y 2025. El estudio From Sanctions Evasion to Money Laundering: The Venezuelan Oil Trading Scheme reconstruyó el 80% de 435 embarques identificados durante 2025. El informe describió mecanismos de intermediación, estructuras empresariales en distintas jurisdicciones y formas de pago que, según la organización, dificultaron seguir el recorrido de los ingresos. También identificó operadores que ya aparecían en negocios petroleros de años anteriores. La continuidad de algunos participantes es una de las alertas que recoge el nuevo mapa de empresas del sector petrolero, con datos al 31 de octubre de 2026. De los 303 bloques petroleros y gasíferos considerados en el análisis, 134 están en manos de empresas privadas y 169 permanecen bajo control de Petróleos de Venezuela (Pdvsa). La organización identifica 63 compañías activas procedentes de 33 países. De ellas, 21 son nuevas en el sector, 11 tienen proyectos en estudio y 15 fueron desplazadas. Entre los nombres que aparecen en esa reorganización está el empresario Alejandro Betancourt López, a quien Transparencia Venezuela identifica como operador en la comercialización de crudo sancionado. Betancourt controla actualmente North American Blue Energy Partner (NABEP), a la que se le asignaron 31 bloques y que reporta una producción de 224.000 barriles diarios. Ver más: Nabep tomará control de Petrocedeño y ampliará su operación petrolera en Venezuela La organización señala que el empresario ha sido objeto de señalamientos relacionados con sobreprecios en la crisis eléctrica, préstamos a Pdvsa y presuntos esquemas de lavado de dinero. De acuerdo con sus registros, mantiene 82 empresas en 21 países. El mapa también recoge otros casos que, a juicio de la ONG, requieren mayor escrutinio. Pacific Coast Energy Co. recibió 12 bloques, aunque Transparencia Venezuela afirma que no ha podido establecer con certeza las capacidades de inversión ni la experiencia reciente de la compañía, así como la identidad de sus beneficiarios finales. También menciona a UCC Oil and Gas, vinculada a licencias en el campo gasífero Loran, y a Primavera Infinita LLC, constituida en 2026 y asignataria del bloque Budare-Elotes. La reorganización también desplazó a nombres vinculados al entorno presidencial, como Carlos Malpica Flores y Ramón Carretero Napolitano en Hainan Breey Energy. La organización registra, además, al menos dos casos de presunta vulneración de derechos de propiedad y unos 15 en los que habrían cambiado las condiciones contractuales sin que se conozcan los procedimientos aplicados. En el comunicado difundido con la presentación del informe, Mercedes De Freitas advirtió que la entrada de nuevos participantes no garantiza por sí sola un cambio en las prácticas del sector. “Que salgan unos operadores y entren otros no limpia el sistema. Si no sabemos quién es el beneficiario final de cada empresa ni bajo qué condiciones recibió los campos, el petróleo sigue siendo un vehículo ideal para legitimar capitales”. La directora de Transparencia Venezuela sostuvo en entrevista con Bloomberg Línea que Pdvsa conserva un papel relevante en el negocio y que todavía no existe información suficiente para seguir el recorrido de los ingresos. Entre los datos que considera necesarios están los volúmenes comercializados, los compradores, los precios, los descuentos aplicados, las condiciones de pago y la administración de los recursos. La preocupación alcanza a los contratos de participación productiva y otros acuerdos con empresas privadas. De Freitas considera que deben publicarse los documentos, los campos asignados y las condiciones negociadas, además de identificarse a los beneficiarios finales de cada compañía. La posibilidad de recuperar los recursos involucrados en las tramas de corrupción representa otro desafío. De Freitas advirtió que no será sencillo devolver a Venezuela la totalidad del dinero desviado, debido a que los fondos suelen fragmentarse, trasladarse entre distintas jurisdicciones y convertirse en activos de diferente naturaleza. Cada país tiene sus propios procedimientos judiciales y mecanismos para congelar, confiscar y devolver esos bienes. Por eso, una investigación o una incautación no se traducen automáticamente en la recuperación de los fondos. Ver más: Machado cuestiona el acuerdo petrolero de Trump, pero apuesta por una alianza de largo plazo con EE.UU. De Freitas también señaló que el país no debería contar con esos recursos como una fuente inmediata para financiar su recuperación económica. Aunque considera necesario continuar las investigaciones y los esfuerzos de cooperación internacional, el rastreo y la restitución de activos pueden prolongarse durante años y no necesariamente permiten recuperar todo el patrimonio comprometido. La organización plantea que Venezuela necesitaría instituciones especializadas para investigar la corrupción y gestionar la recuperación de activos, además de mecanismos independientes que permitan administrar los recursos que eventualmente sean restituidos. La cooperación judicial entre países sería determinante para rastrear los fondos y evitar que queden dispersos en diferentes sistemas financieros. Las dudas sobre la rendición de cuentas también alcanzan la información divulgada por el Gobierno a través de Transparencia Soberana, un portal oficial que fue actualizado el 12 de noviembre por Delcy Rodríguez con un balance de ingresos y egresos correspondiente al período entre enero y noviembre de 2026. Según los datos publicados, los ingresos sumaron US$15.603 millones y los egresos alcanzaron US$14.860 millones. De estos últimos, US$14.710 millones correspondieron a salarios de trabajadores del sector público y pensiones, mientras que US$150,5 millones se destinaron a gastos de funcionamiento del Gobierno. Rodríguez destacó que 99 de cada US$100 desembolsados se dirigieron a esos compromisos laborales sociales. El portal también reportó que US$15.148 millones, equivalentes al 97,1% de los ingresos, provinieron de la venta de petróleo y derivados. Sin embargo, las cifras no permiten conocer con suficiente detalle cómo se distribuyeron los recursos. La propia plataforma señala que su información corresponde al Fondo de Protección Social y al Fondo de Infraestructura Nacional, por lo que no constituye una rendición de cuentas integral de todos los ingresos y gastos del Estado. De Freitas cuestionó precisamente la falta de desagregación. Para la directora de Transparencia Venezuela, no basta con informar cuánto dinero se destinó a salarios y pensiones: es necesario conocer cuántos trabajadores públicos recibieron esos pagos, qué organismos fueron cubiertos, cuántos pensionados están incluidos y qué partidas presupuestarias financiaron los desembolsos. La información también debería permitir distinguir entre salarios y bonificaciones, así como identificar los montos asignados a cada institución. Ese nivel de detalle permitiría contrastar las cifras oficiales con los pagos recibidos por los trabajadores y con las necesidades de servicios públicos como hospitales y centros educativos. Ver más: Altos costos de transporte marítimo reducen demanda de EE.UU. por petróleo venezolano De Freitas planteó, además, que el presupuesto nacional y sus modificaciones deben estar disponibles para consulta pública. De esa manera podría verificarse si los gastos corresponden a las partidas aprobadas y si los cambios presupuestarios siguieron los procedimientos correspondientes. La actualización de Transparencia Soberana coincide con una nueva etapa de supervisión estadounidense sobre los ingresos derivados de la comercialización de recursos venezolanos. Para Transparencia Venezuela, ese mecanismo no sustituye la obligación de las autoridades de explicar cómo se utilizan los fondos ni de publicar información que permita su fiscalización.

Nov 22 : Captain Bruno Fernandes said Manchester United have offered him a new contract but discussions have been put on hold as the club focuses on turning around its poor form. Fernandes' current deal expires at the end of the season, although United hold an option to extend the midfielder's contract by a further year until June 2028, giving the club more time to reach an agreement on fresh terms. "Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on," Fernandes told Sky Sports in an interview published on Sunday. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but because of the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

"The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games." The Portugal international also addressed comments claiming he had demanded more money and a longer deal, saying his priority was to remain at Old Trafford and help restore the club's fortunes. United are third from bottom of the Premier League standings, having won only one of their opening 10 league matches, their worst start to a season in 40 years. "I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United," Fernandes said. "I could have been in a place that's much warmer than Manchester." New manager Mauricio Pochettino, appointed after Michael Carrick was sacked earlier this month, will take charge of his first game when United face fifth-placed Liverpool on Sunday.

item.title: Shiba Inu Team Makes Key GitHub Clarification for ShibaSwap, Shibarium
item.description: "Shib.io is home to both Shibarium and ShibaSwap," Shiba Inu developer and long-time community member Mazrael said, citing the project’s public Git repository as evidence of the longstanding ...
item.content:encoded:
News / U.Today / Shiba Inu Team Makes Key GitHub Clarification for ShibaSwap, Shibarium

Shiba Inu Team Makes Key GitHub Clarification for ShibaSwap, Shibarium 2 min read

SHIBUSD BONEUSD "Shib.io is home to both Shibarium and ShibaSwap," Shiba Inu developer and long-time community member Mazrael said, citing the project’s public Git repository as evidence of the longstanding relationship. Mazrael recently spoke about the link between the official web presence of the Shiba Inu ecosystem and its decentralized platforms in a post, stating that the information has been consistent since the launch of ShibaSwap.

Mazrael.shib @Mazrael_shib

@Heisenbergiqr3 @tacitfi @randhindi @LCSHIB @Shibtoken https://t.co/RP8CH8r1zW is home of Shibarium and Shibaswap as indicated in our public git that has not changed since Shibaswap and is the same git for shibarium

Nov 21, 2026

Mazrael says the public Git repository has not changed since the launch of ShibaSwap and is the same repository that is used for Shibarium. The clarification seems intended to quell confusion on Shiba Inu's official channels as legacy domains become decommissioned. He pointed to the project’s public Git as proof that Shib.io is the home of Shibarium and ShibaSwap. The clarification strengthens the link among Shib.io, ShibaSwap and Shibarium, two key components of the Shiba Inu ecosystem. Mazrael's reference to the unchanged public Git repository also highlights the team's position that this connection is not a recent development but part of the project's established infrastructure. In the latest development for Shibarium, Mazrael announced that CreateX is now live on the Shiba Inu Layer 2. Shiba Inu price rebounds Shiba Inu has climbed back above $0.0000035, recovering from Saturday's low of $0.00000337, its weakest level in years. It’s trading near $0.0000036, up 3.23% in the last 24 hours. The broader crypto market is seeing a short-term rebound, but it does not fully establish that the decline has ended. According to Santiment, “Stablecoin Whale Dry Powder Continues Shrinking Across Crypto.” The largest tracked stablecoin whales are holding far less dry powder than before, Santiment stated, noting that since the start of the year, USDT balances on Ethereum held by the top 100 whales have fallen by $15.14 billion (-21.1%) and USDC (on Ethereum) balances are down $6.72 billion (-23.7%). Stablecoins are crypto’s ready-to-deploy cash, so large whale balances can represent potential buying power for BTC and altcoins. Falling balances can mean funds were deployed, redeemed, transferred elsewhere, or moved outside these tracked wallets. Either way, having less USDT and USDC concentrated among major holders means less obvious dry powder waiting on the sidelines.
